knowledgeAnswers.rationale: The lesson says to count only billable hours, since travel, collection, admin, training, PPE time and leave are not billable. Building the rate from billable hours lets the work that is billed cover the costs and income.
The lesson says travel, collection and set-up do not shrink with the size of the item, so a minimum charge covers that fixed time. The other options contradict the lesson.

The lesson says to set the rate from your own costs and billable hours and to check it against your own log. A single national average, a friend's rate or a bidding-site listing is not the recommended check.

practicalCriteria: Learner calculates billable hours from a one-month log, showing each non-billable deduction.
Learner builds a base rate from a worksheet of annual costs and an income target, showing the calculation.
Learner sets a minimum charge for a short job and writes the wording the client will see before the visit.
passRule: 80% on knowledge checks; practical sign-off separate
stopWorkCriteria: Stop work if procedure step 1 is not done: Estimate the paid working hours in a year, then subtract travel, collection, admin, training, PPE time and leave to find the billable hours.
